name: Nakajima Ki-43-II Oscar
blurb: A light Army fighter with retractable main gear, two 12.7 mm cowl guns and, in Dev only, two bomb racks. Its speed and climb come from one Allied intelligence sheet, and its stall speed, roll rate and handling are estimates; the drawn model's variant is unconfirmed.
history:
The Nakajima Ki-43 Hayabusa ("peregrine falcon"), the Army Type 1 Fighter, was a single-engine land-based fighter of the Imperial Japanese Army Air Service. Its Allied reporting name was "Oscar", but American pilots often called it the "Army Zero" for its resemblance to the Navy's A6M. It was the Army's first all-metal fighter with an enclosed cockpit and retractable landing gear.

The Ki-43 entered service in October 1941, just before Japan entered the war, and served on every front the Army air service fought on. Like the Zero, it was light and relatively easy to fly, and improved versions followed in December 1942 and the summer of 1944.

What this entry models: the Ki-43-II figures (span, weight, engine ratings, top speed, climb and dive limit) come from a single Allied intelligence sheet of December 1944, which disagrees with other published figures (for example 330 mph at 13,000 ft against the sheet's 347 mph at 20,000 ft). The stall speeds, roll rate, gear timing and control feel are estimates scaled from the Zero. The bombs offered in Dev are the Hellcat's 1,000 lb store, far heavier than the 66 to 220 lb the type carried. The drawn model may be a different variant from the one flown.

sources.title: Ki-43-II Oscar 2, TAIC Manual sheets 152A-2 and 152A-3, December 1944 (Wayback capture of wwiiaircraftperformance.org)
